title: Fixtures, factories and test data sets

videos.script: Every test runs inside a small world. A database with a schema. A directory with a file in it. A server listening on a port. {{world}} This lesson is about building that world, and about the data you put in it. {{data}} First, fixtures. A fixture sets the world up before a test and takes it down after, whether the test passed or not. You will watch pytest do it, test by test. {{fixtures}} Then the trade every slow suite is tempted by. Share the world between tests and the suite gets faster. It also gets a test that passes alone and fails beside the others. You will see exactly that happen. {{scope}} Then the data. A factory builds valid data and lets each test name only what it is about. A table keeps the shop's published prices as a file the business can read. {{factories}} Then two things that make a test give different answers on different days. The clock, and randomness. Both become inputs. {{time}} After that, a library that chooses the inputs for you, and finds a bug in two cents split four ways. {{properties}} And one rule to close. Test data is made, never copied from production. {{privacy}}
